overview: The Hillsborough disaster at Liverpool’s FA Cup semi-final against Nottingham Forest on 15 April 1989 ultimately claimed the lives of 97 Liverpool supporters. The match was abandoned. Liverpool’s competitive fixtures resumed in May, and the semi-final was replayed at Old Trafford, where they won 3–1.

Liverpool won the FA Cup by beating Everton 3–2 after extra time at Wembley. John Aldridge scored the opener and substitute Ian Rush scored twice in extra time. In the league, Liverpool finished level with Arsenal on 76 points and goal difference, but lost the title on goals scored after Arsenal won 2–0 at Anfield in the final match. Michael Thomas scored the decisive late goal.

Rush had returned from Juventus, while Aldridge finished as leading scorer with 31 competitive goals. Liverpool also won the Charity Shield against Wimbledon. West Ham ended their League Cup run in the fourth round, and Arsenal beat them in the Football League Centenary Trophy semi-final.

sources.claims: The disaster at the Liverpool–Nottingham Forest FA Cup semi-final on 15 April 1989 ultimately claimed 97 lives. This is the eventual death toll, not a claim that every victim died that day.

sources.label: 1988–89 FA Cup: semi-final context
sources.claims: Limited corroborating scope: the Hillsborough semi-final was abandoned and rescheduled for 7 May. The eventual death toll is sourced from Liverpool FC; the completed result and venue from LFChistory.

researchNotes: Overview evidence: paragraph 1 — lfc-hillsborough, facup-season-context and lfch-games; paragraph 2 — lfc-fa-cup, lfc-manager, rsssf-league and lfch-games; paragraph 3 — lfch-transfers, lfch-scorers, lfc-aldridge, lfc-shield and lfch-games.
The 97 figure is the eventual Hillsborough death toll. It must not be described as 97 deaths on the day. Football results are reported separately without a redemption narrative.
The final table gives both clubs 76 points and +37 goal difference: Arsenal scored 73 and Liverpool 65. This resolves the title on goals scored, not goal difference.

The two full-match Centenary Trophy fixtures are included in the competitive season record. Aldridge’s September 1989 departure belongs to 1989–90. Unverified retirement dates and post-release destinations have been omitted from the selected transfer list.
